title: README for the published package: install and run under Node via npm (must land before the v0.1.0 tag)
description: README.md ships in the tarball and becomes the npm page, and a published version cannot be replaced. As of dev 1d462b6 line 22 says 'Not published yet — the package is private until first release', the License section says 'Glyph is private until first release', and 'Run it' covers only a checkout with Bun. Rewrite for the published package: install and run under Node >= 24 with npm i -g @opum-ai/glyph and glyph, keep the checkout-with-Bun route as the development path, and make every link resolve for a registry reader (relative links and docs paths do not). README-only. Must land before any v0.1.0 tag, and the tag must name a commit that contains it, because the tag check compares only the version. Opus review (public surface and release path).

acceptanceCriteria.text: the Run it section gives the install and run commands for a registry reader (npm i -g @opum-ai/glyph, then glyph callers ...) with the Node >= 24 requirement, and keeps the Bun checkout route under a development heading (proof: README diff read at the head)
no sentence says the package is private or unpublished (proof: grep -n -i -E "private|not published" README.md returns nothing that describes the package state)
every link and path in README.md resolves for someone reading it on npmjs.com: no repository-relative link that 404s there (proof: a recorded link check listing each link and the URL it resolves to)
every example command in the Run it section runs against the packed tarball installed under node (proof: the Package job runs, or a recorded local run of, each README example from the installed copy)
the README example for --stream still matches the fixture byte for byte (proof: the existing README stream test passes unmodified)
the change landed before any v0.1.0 tag exists (proof: git ls-remote --tags origin empty at merge, and the tag later names a commit containing the new README)

implementationNotes: 2026-11-23 Opus review of glyph-cli#104 (homepage -> https://github.com/opum-ai/glyph-cli#readme), reviewer claude-opus-5-5 (spawn-model MATCH, read by the leader from its transcript): APPROVE at head 7a2aa6192babc49a85702973cb2ea7720f71693e; landed as 5f8673a. Non-blocking points as relayed: (a) the reviewer read files only and ran no git, bun, npm or gh; 'nothing else changed' is inferred from the PR file list; (b) the homepage, bugs and repository URLs return 404 to the public until the visibility flip, which the ruling accepted; (c) docs/adr/0002 links to opum-ai/opum-doc, which may be private and dead for npm readers (README.md itself has no opum-doc link at head 0cc83ba; the reviewer's README.md:212 pointer did not match the file); (d) follow-up filed as a low-priority task, not started: assert homepage in test/packaging.test.ts.
finalSummary: Superseded by GCLI-87: the README for npm landed there (npm install, Node >= 24, no private wording); opum-doc read the tagged v0.1.0 README and confirmed it.
